content: ISBT 128 is a globally standardized system designed for the identification, labeling, and processing of human blood, tissue, and cellular therapy products. The acronym ISBT stands for the International Society of Blood Transfusion, and the number 128 refers to the barcode symbology known as Code 128. This system was first introduced in 1994 as Version 1, with the goal of replacing the older ABC Codabar and other similar Codabar-based standards used in transfusion medicine at the time. The new system provided a more secure barcode symbology capable of encoding more detailed information. The development of ISBT 128 involved collaboration between the ISBT working group on automation and data processing, the American Association of Blood Banks (AABB), the American Red Cross (ARC), the Department of Defense, and the Health Industry Manufacturers Association. This collaboration led to the adoption of ISBT 128 as an international standard. To oversee its implementation and management, the International Council for Commonality in Blood Banking Automation (ICCBBA) was established. The AABB mandated that all AABB-accredited blood banks implement ISBT 128 by May 1, 2008. The ISBT 128 system enhances standardization in transfusion medicine by assigning a unique donation identification number to each blood product. This number includes a collection facility code, enabling precise identification and tracking of products worldwide. The system ensures that specific products and blood treatment processes are consistently labeled in the same manner. The ISBT 128 barcode is highly efficient, allowing a significant amount of information to be encoded in a compact space. It also includes an internal check digit to prevent barcode misreads. The barcode contains critical information such as ABO/Rh blood type and product codes, followed by specific unit details. The label is divided into four quadrants for clarity: the donor ID (unit number) is printed in the upper left quadrant, the ABO/Rh blood type in the upper right quadrant, the product code in the lower left quadrant, and the expiration date/time (down to the hour and minute) in the lower right quadrant. Additionally, the lower right quadrant may include information about special testing, such as antigen or CMV status.
